narrative:
Bailiff Reyes is not, it turns out, hard to find - word of hostages on a crown road travels fast in his direction specifically. He's already assembling a response when you reach him, jaw set in the particular grim line of a man who quotes statutes because feelings complicate enforcement.

@Bailiff Reyes: A tax collector's assistant taking hostages over a grievance with the crown. There's a tidy little irony in that I'd almost admire, if people weren't currently at risk because of it. You're offering to help, or you're offering to get in my way. Which is it?

narrative:
Up close, he looks less like the composed extortionist from your first meeting and more like a man who's gambled everything on a play he's no longer sure was wise. The formal phrasing is still there, but it's fraying at the edges.

@Tollkeeper: Ah. You. I confess I hoped it might be you, and dreaded it in equal measure. Circumstances have escalated somewhat since our last transaction, as I'm sure you've noticed.

narrative:
You find the actual argument underneath the theater - not really about silver at all, not anymore, but about a man who lost everything to a system he used to serve and has no idea how to be heard by it otherwise. It takes longer than either of you expect, but somewhere in the middle of it, he lowers the knife he'd been holding more for effect than intent.

@Tollkeeper: I don't - I don't actually want to hurt anyone. I want someone from that court to look at what they did to me and call it what it was. This was a very poor way of arranging that. I see that now, rather late.

@Tollkeeper: Words. Everyone always has words. I had words too, once, in front of a court that didn't listen to a single one of them. Forgive me if I've lost patience with the format.

narrative:
It's not clean and it's not quiet, but it's fast - the hired guards break and run at the first real sign of resistance, leaving the Tollkeeper alone and considerably less composed than he'd like to be, disarmed before he's fully processed the fight starting.

Ferrick, watching from where the hostages huddled, lets out a low whistle. @Ferrick: Remind me never to leave you holding my coin pouch AND assume you're harmless. Might've undersold you rather badly, in hindsight.

narrative: Whatever composure existed at this roadblock is gone now, replaced with the particular chaos of a situation nobody, including the man who started it, still has full control over. A hostage cries out. A guard's crossbow wavers between targets that keep moving. The Tollkeeper himself looks less like a schemer now and more like a man watching his own plan become something he never actually wanted it to be.

@Tollkeeper: I don't - this isn't the outcome I planned for, in any version of how today could have gone. Thank you. I don't imagine that means much, from someone who tried to rob you for a toll not long ago. I mean it regardless.

narrative:
It's a strange offer to make to a man who tried to rob you twice, and stranger still that he accepts it - something in him finally cracking open at being offered a path that isn't punishment or forgiveness exactly, just a plain, practical second chance.

@Tollkeeper: I was a tax officer once. Good with numbers, actually, before I became - whatever this was. If there's honest work that wants a man good with numbers and short on better options, I find I am, unexpectedly, willing to take it.
